audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's challenge to retribution theology: hidden times, social injustice, exploitation of poor/widows/orphans, night crimes, divine delay, and unresolved wicked prosperity.

verses.restored: Why are times not stored up by Shaddai, and why do those who know him not see his days?

familiar.text: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?

modern.text: “Why does the Almighty not reserve times for judgment? Why may those who know Him never see His days?

original.text: מַדּ֗וּעַ מִ֭שַּׁדַּי לֹא נִצְפְּנ֣וּ עִתִּ֑ים וידעו לֹא חָ֥זוּ יָמָֽיו

verses.restored: People move boundary markers; they seize flocks and pasture them.

familiar.text: Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.

modern.text: Men move boundary stones; they pasture stolen flocks.

original.text: גְּבֻל֥וֹת יַשִּׂ֑יגוּ עֵ֥דֶר גָּ֝זְל֗וּ וַיִּרְעֽוּ

verses.restored: They drive away the donkey of orphans; they take the widow’s ox as pledge.

familiar.text: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

modern.text: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless and take the widow’s ox in pledge.

original.text: חֲמ֣וֹר יְתוֹמִ֣ים יִנְהָ֑גוּ יַ֝חְבְּל֗וּ שׁ֣וֹר אַלְמָנָֽה

verses.restored: They turn the needy aside from the way; the poor of the earth hide together.

familiar.text: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

modern.text: They push the needy off the road and force all the poor of the land into hiding.

original.text: יַטּ֣וּ אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים מִדָּ֑רֶךְ יַ֥חַד חֻ֝בְּא֗וּ עֲנִיֵּי אָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Look, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their work, seeking food; the desert gives bread for their young.

familiar.text: Behold, as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness yieldeth food for them and for their children.

modern.text: Indeed, like wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work foraging for food; the wasteland is food for their children.

original.text: הֵ֤ן פְּרָאִ֨ים בַּֽמִּדְבָּ֗ר יָצְא֣וּ בְּ֭פָעֳלָם מְשַׁחֲרֵ֣י לַטָּ֑רֶף עֲרָבָ֥ה ל֥וֹ לֶ֝֗חֶם לַנְּעָרִֽים

verses.restored: In the field they harvest fodder, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.

familiar.text: They reap every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.

modern.text: They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.

original.text: בַּ֭שָּׂדֶה בְּלִיל֣וֹ יקצירו וְכֶ֖רֶם רָשָׁ֣ע יְלַקֵּֽשׁוּ

verses.restored: They spend the night naked, without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.

familiar.text: They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that they have no covering in the cold.

modern.text: Without clothing, they spend the night naked; they have no covering against the cold.

original.text: עָר֣וֹם יָ֭לִינוּ מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת בַּקָּרָֽה

verses.restored: They are wet with mountain rain and cling to the rock for lack of shelter.

familiar.text: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.

modern.text: Drenched by mountain rains, they huddle against the rocks for want of shelter.

original.text: מִזֶּ֣רֶם הָרִ֣ים יִרְטָ֑בוּ וּֽמִבְּלִ֥י מַ֝חְסֶ֗ה חִבְּקוּ צֽוּר

verses.restored: The orphan is torn from the breast, and a pledge is taken from the poor.

familiar.text: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.

modern.text: The fatherless infant is snatched from the breast; the nursing child of the poor is seized for a debt.

original.text: יִ֭גְזְלוּ מִשֹּׁ֣ד יָת֑וֹם וְֽעַל עָנִ֥י יַחְבֹּֽלוּ

verses.restored: They go about naked, without clothing; hungry, they carry sheaves.

familiar.text: They cause him to go naked without clothing, and they take away the sheaf from the hungry;

modern.text: Without clothing, they wander about naked. They carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.

original.text: עָר֣וֹם הִ֭לְּכוּ בְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וּ֝רְעֵבִ֗ים נָ֣שְׂאוּ עֹֽמֶר

verses.restored: Between their walls they press oil; they tread winepresses, yet thirst.

familiar.text: Which make oil within their walls, and tread their winepresses, and suffer thirst.

modern.text: They crush olives within their walls; they tread the winepresses, but go thirsty.

original.text: בֵּין שׁוּרֹתָ֥ם יַצְהִ֑ירוּ יְקָבִ֥ים דָּ֝רְכ֗וּ וַיִּצְמָֽאוּ

verses.restored: From the city people groan, and the soul of the wounded cries out; yet the Divine does not charge it as folly.

familiar.text: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly to them.

modern.text: From the city, men groan, and the souls of the wounded cry out, yet God charges no one with wrongdoing.

original.text: מֵ֘עִ֤יר מְתִ֨ים יִנְאָ֗קוּ וְנֶֽפֶשׁ חֲלָלִ֥ים תְּשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וֶ֝אֱל֗וֹהַּ לֹא יָשִׂ֥ים תִּפְלָֽה

verses.restored: They are among rebels against light; they do not recognize its ways and do not remain in its paths.

familiar.text: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.

modern.text: Then there are those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways or staying on its paths.

original.text: הֵ֤מָּה הָיוּ֮ בְּֽמֹרְדֵ֫י א֥וֹר לֹֽא הִכִּ֥ירוּ דְרָכָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָ֝שְׁב֗וּ בִּנְתִיבֹתָֽיו

verses.restored: At dawn the murderer rises; he kills the poor and needy, and in the night he is like a thief.

familiar.text: The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.

modern.text: When daylight is gone, the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy; in the night he is like a thief.

original.text: לָא֡וֹר יָ֘ק֤וּם רוֹצֵ֗חַ יִֽקְטָל עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְי֑וֹן וּ֝בַלַּ֗יְלָה יְהִ֣י כַגַּנָּֽב

verses.restored: The eye of the adulterer waits for twilight, saying, No eye will see me, and he sets a covering on his face.

familiar.text: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.

modern.text: The eye of the adulterer watches for twilight. Thinking, ‘No eye will see me,’ he covers his face.

original.text: וְעֵ֤ין נֹאֵ֨ף שָׁ֤מְרָֽה נֶ֣שֶׁף לֵ֭אמֹר לֹא תְשׁוּרֵ֣נִי עָ֑יִן וְסֵ֖תֶר פָּנִ֣ים יָשִֽׂים

verses.restored: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in; they do not know light.

familiar.text: In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.

modern.text: In the dark they dig through houses; by day they shut themselves in, never to experience the light.

original.text: חָתַ֥ר בַּחֹ֗שֶׁךְ בָּ֫תִּ֥ים יוֹמָ֥ם חִתְּמוּ לָ֗מוֹ לֹא יָ֥דְעוּ אֽוֹר

verses.restored: For deep darkness is morning to all of them, because they know the terrors of deep darkness.

familiar.text: For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death: if one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.

modern.text: For to them, deep darkness is their morning; surely they are friends with the terrors of darkness!

original.text: כִּ֤י יַחְדָּ֨ו בֹּ֣קֶר לָ֣מוֹ צַלְמָ֑וֶת כִּֽי יַ֝כִּ֗יר בַּלְה֥וֹת צַלְמָֽוֶת

verses.restored: They are swift on the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth; no one turns toward the way of the vineyards.

familiar.text: He is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.

modern.text: They are but foam on the surface of the water; their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one turns toward their vineyards.

original.text: קַֽל ה֤וּא עַל פְּנֵי מַ֗יִם תְּקֻלַּ֣ל חֶלְקָתָ֣ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא יִ֝פְנֶה דֶּ֣רֶךְ כְּרָמִֽים

verses.restored: Drought and heat steal snow-waters; Sheol steals those who have sinned.

familiar.text: Drought and heat consume the snow waters: so doth the grave those which have sinned.

modern.text: As drought and heat consume the melting snow, so Sheol steals those who have sinned.

original.text: צִיָּ֤ה גַם חֹ֗ם יִגְזְל֥וּ מֵֽימֵי שֶׁ֗לֶג שְׁא֣וֹל חָטָֽאוּ

verses.restored: The womb forgets him; worms feed sweetly on him; he is remembered no more, and injustice is broken like a tree.

familiar.text: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.

modern.text: The womb forgets them; the worm feeds on them; they are remembered no more. So injustice is like a broken tree.

original.text: יִשְׁכָּ֘חֵ֤הוּ רֶ֨חֶם מְתָ֘ק֤וֹ רִמָּ֗ה ע֥וֹד לֹֽא יִזָּכֵ֑ר וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֖ר כָּעֵ֣ץ עַוְלָֽה

verses.restored: He feeds on the barren woman who does not bear and does no good to the widow.

familiar.text: He evil entreateth the barren that beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.

modern.text: They prey on the barren and childless, and show no kindness to the widow.

original.text: רֹעֶ֣ה עֲ֭קָרָה לֹ֣א תֵלֵ֑ד וְ֝אַלְמָנָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְיֵטִֽיב

verses.restored: Yet he draws the mighty by his power; he rises up, and no one is sure of life.

familiar.text: He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life.

modern.text: Yet by His power, God drags away the mighty; though rising up, they have no assurance of life.

original.text: וּמָשַׁ֣ךְ אַבִּירִ֣ים בְּכֹח֑וֹ יָ֝ק֗וּם וְֽלֹא יַאֲמִ֥ין בַּֽחַיִּֽין

verses.restored: He gives him security, and he leans on it; yet his eyes are on their ways.

familiar.text: Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes are upon their ways.

modern.text: He gives them a sense of security, but His eyes are on their ways.

original.text: יִתֶּן ל֣וֹ לָ֭בֶטַח וְיִשָּׁעֵ֑ן וְ֝עֵינֵ֗יהוּ עַל דַּרְכֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: They are lifted a little, then are no more; they are brought low, gathered like all others, and cut off like heads of grain.

familiar.text: They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

modern.text: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.

original.text: ר֤וֹמּוּ מְּעַ֨ט וְֽאֵינֶ֗נּוּ וְֽהֻמְּכ֗וּ כַּכֹּ֥ל יִקָּפְצ֑וּן וּכְרֹ֖אשׁ שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת יִמָּֽלוּ

verses.restored: If it is not so, who will make me a liar and make my word nothing?

familiar.text: And if it be not so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?

modern.text: If this is not so, then who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?”

original.text: וְאִם לֹ֣א אֵ֭פוֹ מִ֣י יַכְזִיבֵ֑נִי וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְ֝אַ֗ל מִלָּתִֽי
